description.narrative: The proposed IDF grant will support the IAAC in its core mandate of corruption prevention and monitoring. It will have three components: Component 1: Effective implementation of the Asset and Income and Conflict of Interest Declarations. As per the anti-corruption law and the conflict of interest law, public servants are required to annually prepare these declarations and the IAAC oversees the process. Currently over 50,000 public officials file these declarations. The IAAC has limited ability to analyze these declarations, and there is still limited understanding of the recently passed Conflict of Interest Law. Component 2: Improving inter-agency cooperation with other key agencies, such as the tax authority and the Office of the Prosecutor General, which is necessary to effectively analyze the accuracy of the asset and income declarations, and to investigate and prosecute corruption cases; as well as line ministries so that the IAAC is viewed as a partner in fighting corruption. Component 3: Strengthening monitoring and evaluation. The anti-corruption law requires the IAAC to measure progress in reducing corruption and to this end the agency developed the Mongolia Corruption Index (MCI), a composite indicator of corruption based on household and business corruption perception surveys. Two rounds of such surveys have been completed (in 2009 and 2011). The agency however, need support in improvement of the methodology of the MCI and corruption risk assessments of ministries and agencies and in enhancing its capacity to analyze the surveys.
